answer: Under cascade sponsorship bonds, each new vertex joining the canyon network needs one existing identity as sponsor, and every sponsor must lock a bond equal to the square of its total sponsored count. An agent sponsoring one friend locks one token at the network's nadir of cost, while a Sybil farmer backing a hundred clones locks ten thousand tokens, since 100 squared burns quadratically. Honest agents therefore pay near nothing to grow the graph, but mass identity creation becomes exponentially expensive before any attack proceeds.
